thread:
Maya: Quick follow-up on the staged variant/resilience idea — can we treat the canary as a first-class variant with its own QoS and an automatic safety-net policy?
Evan: +1. Means runtime needs to keep per-variant metadata (probe hooks, budgets) not just a single routing table.
Jia: Curious about signals — do we only look at latency/errors or also model-quality signals (e.g., hallucination_score)?
Maya: We should include a small quality signal. For text gen, weirdness/hallucination detection from the eval model can be a weak signal combined with latency and 5m error rate. Not a show-stopper alone but useful for multi-signal aborts.
Khalid: Tradeoff: pushing more logic into control plane makes rollouts auditable and testable, but adds RTT on decision loops. If we keep runtime decision simple (local thresholds + probe tokens) we reduce latency.
Evan: Proposal: decision split — control plane owns long-lived policies (policy DSL + safe defaults), runtime evaluates fast probes and short-window metrics. Control plane can push updated thresholds.
Maya: That fits. Also want session affinity behavior: ephemeral session pinning to canary variant for N requests, but fallback on error should be immediate.
Khalid: Implementation sketch: runtime maintains a lightweight state machine per session: {state: pinned|probing|fallback, attempts, last_probe_ts}. Control plane supplies policy blob:
```
variant_policy: {
  traffic_pct: 5,
  probe_window_s: 30,
  max_errors: 3,
  quality_abort_threshold: 0.8
}
```
ops-bot: deploy-bot: just ran a dry-check of policy DSL syntax for the example above — OK.
Jia: For quality signals we need to define a coarse score; we'll use existing eval-model endpoint and average across first 3 responses in probe window. Might be noisy but workable.
Evan: Edge case: downstream retries from clients can amplify traffic spikes. Runtime should annotate requests that are retries so control plane can exclude them from traffic_pct accounting.
Maya: Good call. Also we should guarantee a fallback path that preserves schema compatibility (model variant must expose same function signatures).
Khalid: Long-term refactor: move policy DSL into a shared library used by control plane, CLI, and runtime so tests can validate semantics once. Short-term: implement a v0 policy parser in control plane and a tiny runtime evaluator.
Jia: I'll draft the probe/eval contract and a minimal quality scorer by Friday.
Khalid: I'll prototype the session state machine in the runtime and emit metric tags: variant, session_state, probe_result.
Maya: Action items: @Jia - probe contract & quality scorer; @Khalid - runtime state machine prototype; @Evan - integrate policy push API + audit log schema; I'll own rollout playbook and abort thresholds doc. :white_check_mark:
Evan: Sounds good. Quick note: include an escape hatch to immediately shift 100% to primary for emergencies (manual or automated).
Maya: Yep — emergency_cutover: true in the policy and baked into the CLI `redwood rollout abort`.
ops-bot: incident-bot: when emergency_cutover flips, alert team and freeze further auto-rollouts.
Khalid: Will instrument a few synthetic probes to validate that fallback path doesn't regress latency under load.
Jia: ok I'll add e2e tests that simulate noisy quality signals + client retries.
Maya: Thanks everyone — will collect these and open RFC follow-up with the prototype links by Monday. :rocket:
